scope: Cross-repository runtime companion measurement using Agent-authenticated installations.

Fresh public kernel admission and instance at each boundary; one warmup and five whole-conversation samples per process; three rotating processes/format/window and two windows planned.
cases.scope: Generator, scheduler, queens/search, shallow, reentrant and suspending cleanup; not the complete matrix.

qualification: Expected source results and effect traces are recomputed before timing, and fixture hashes are checked. Fresh kernel admission/instance per boundary; one warmup and five whole-conversation samples/process, three rotating processes/format/window, two windows. Replies and searched branches are unchanged. verdict: Queens BFS improves versus BPC1 in both windows; DFS ranges overlap. Generator, shallow, reentrant and suspending cleanup regress, while scheduler results are noisy and do not establish improvement. Portable State sizes increase. Allocation/copy corroboration for BFS and remaining workloads are still required.

hostAdmissionCandidate.verdict: All seven whole-conversation cases improve versus BPC1 in both windows under this repeated-factory workload. Cold first-call costs and native interpreter regressions remain separate; this does not close the entire required matrix.

workReplay.qualification: Instrumented semantic qualification outside timed windows. Counts are WebAssembly API calls, not claims about internal engine code generation.
workReplay.observations: Both execute 29 fresh guest instances across the seven verified source cases; candidate avoids repeated compile API calls through the weak admitted-module entry.
